newsitem.title: USA: Expert in Simpson case says DNA evidence unreliable.
newsitem.headline: Expert in Simpson case says DNA evidence unreliable.

text.p: An expert testifying in O.J. Simpson's civil trial told jurors Thursday that DNA evidence apparently implicating the ex-football star in the murders of his ex-wife and her friend could not be relied upon.
"I believe there is an unacceptable risk or chance, by the way these samples were handled, of there being cross-contamination," Dr John Gerdes said.

His testimony came as Simpson's defence team pursued its two-pronged theory that Los Angeles Police Department forensic experts botched the collection and testing of hair and blood samples and that evidence was planted by police to frame the former athlete.

Gerdes, the clinical director of a Denver DNA lab and one of the country's leading authorities in the field, said tests carried out at the LAPD's crime lab could not be trusted because of the way the samples were collected and the way the tests were conducted.
"I feel that with the sample collection and manipulation and the PCR setup and protocols (at the lab), there is a risk of contamination," he said. PCR is one form of DNA testing.

Gerdes said DNA testing in a hospital setting was far more reliable than testing samples taken from a crime scene because samples obtained in a hospital were "sterile" where crime scene samples were "dirty."

In addition, Gerdes said, such samples had to be collected on cloth "swatches," placed in bags, taken out and dried, and then placed in other bags, with each manipulation increasing the risk of one sample being cross-contaminated by another.

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman by a criminal court jury in October, 1995. He is now being sued by the families of the victims in the civil wrongful death case.
